thread:
Sean Gallagher: Seeing latency + 5xx spike in us-east. Anyone on? paging thread.

incident-bot: Context bundle (beta) for INC-2147
- Service: inference-gateway
- Regions: us-east
- Start window: last 30m

Deploys (collector: deploys) ✅
• 17m ago: inference-gateway v2025.02.12-rc3 (rollout 100%) <https://github.com/redwood/commit/9f2c1d3|commit> <https://github.com/redwood/pull/18452|PR #18452>

Config diffs (collector: config-diff) ✅
• routing.policy.max_concurrency: 1400 -> 2000
• rate_limit.tier_standard.rps: 1200 -> 1200 (no change)

Saturation snapshot (collector: saturation) ⚠️ partial
• ERROR: metrics backend query exceeded time budget (8s). Possible ingestion lag.
• Tried: gpu_queue_depth, scheduler_contention, throttled_requests
• Next steps: check saturation dashboard directly: <https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/rt-sat-us-east|Saturation / us-east>

Rafael Mendes: got it. looking at dashboard now.

Aisha Bello: :eyes: this is the exact failure mode we saw in the last game day. bot posts but saturation is basically useless without telling us what’s missing.

Miles Thornton: can confirm grafana panels are empty-ish rn too. looks like metrics are ~3-4 min behind.

metrics-bot: Alert: telemetry_ingest_lag_high
- cluster: prod-us-east
- lag_seconds_p95: 238
- started: 1707764922

Rafael Mendes: ok so it’s not just bot. we still need the bot to be *clearer* here.

Sean Gallagher: agreed. right now it says “partial” but doesn’t tell you whether it’s stale data vs no data vs query timed out.

Jacob Stein: yeah saturation collector currently does a live query w/ an 8s timeout. if prom/thanos is behind, we end up timing out or returning empty series.

Allison Grant: can we make it fail-open with “last known good” snapshot + a big STALE banner? even 3-5 min old is better than nothing during triage.

Caleb Johnson: careful: last-known-good across region/service is tricky. but we can cache per (service, region) for a short TTL and include `observed_at`.

Miles Thornton: +1. even “observed_at=17:42:10Z (stale by 4m)” is actionable.

Rafael Mendes: the other thing: error section should list exactly what query failed + what label set it used. right now it’s too hand-wavy.

Aisha Bello: + include a one-liner like “metrics ingestion lag detected (p95=238s) → expect saturation data to be stale/missing.” that would build trust.

Sean Gallagher: Jacob can we tweak collector to:
1) never block posting entire bundle
2) render a dedicated “Collector status” section at bottom w/ errors
3) saturation: if query times out, try smaller window (e.g. last 5m) or reduce series cardinality

Jacob Stein: 1 is true today (bundle assembly continues), but the rendering is confusing.
2 we can do. per-collector status block w/ reason + hint.
3 we can add a fallback path: if `range=30m` fails, retry `range=10m` and drop per-model label.

Logan Wright: dropping per-model label is good. the current queries explode when model label cardinality spikes.

Allison Grant: also distinguish:
- timeout
- empty result
- stale (timestamp older than now - threshold)
- permission/redaction (in restricted mode)

Rafael Mendes: yes. “empty result” is different from “timed out”. empty might mean not saturated.

Miles Thornton: and if empty because no series matched labels, that’s usually a bug (wrong service name / region tag).

Jacob Stein: makes sense. we already parse service/region from incident metadata, but when service aliasing happens we miss.

Sean Gallagher: fwiw here it found deploy + config diff fine, so service/region mapping looks ok.

Aisha Bello: question: should saturation collector explicitly say “telemetry ingest lag detected” if that alert is firing? can we query that too (low-cardinality) and attach it?

Caleb Johnson: we can, but please don’t add another dependency that can time out. maybe use the same query response headers (thanos has `X-Thanos-Downsampled`)… or simplest: query a single metric `telemetry_ingest_lag_seconds_p95` which is cheap.

Logan Wright: if we do it, do it with a strict 1-2s budget and if it fails, don’t spam.

Rafael Mendes: also formatting request: if saturation fails, the bot should still give a link to the *exact* dashboard filtered to service+region, not the generic one.

incident-bot: (debug) saturation dashboard link parameters unavailable (service filter key missing) - using fallback link.

Sean Gallagher: lol there it is. “service filter key missing” should be in the main error section, not debug.

Jacob Stein: yeah that’s on me; I left some stuff in debug-only bc we were worried about noise.

Aisha Bello: in an incident thread, i’d rather see a concise error like:
“Saturation: FAILED (timeout 8s). Metrics ingest lag p95=238s. Tried queries: gpu_queue_depth{region=us-east,service=inference-gateway}. Next: open dashboard (filtered) or run /incidentbot saturation --window 5m.”

Miles Thornton: +1. responders can ignore it if they want, but at least it’s explicit.

Rafael Mendes: and it should not claim “partial” unless it actually has some data. partial should mean “some metrics returned; some failed.”

Jacob Stein: good point. we’re currently marking partial if any metric errors; even if 0/3 succeeded.

Allison Grant: can we standardize wording?
- OK
- PARTIAL (x/y succeeded)
- FAILED (0/y)

Sean Gallagher: + add “evidence window” per collector.

Caleb Johnson: the “stale but present” case should be OK/PARTIAL with `observed_at`. not FAILED.

Logan Wright: and show the newest sample timestamp you got back. it’s the fastest way to spot lag.

Rafael Mendes: action item: Jacob can you open a Linear ticket for these rendering + retry behaviors? we can reference this thread.

Jacob Stein: yep will do. (this likely lands in ENG-2845 / ENG-2844 scope)

Sean Gallagher: thank you. meanwhile for this incident: config diff shows max_concurrency bumped 1400 -> 2000. that could correlate. let’s consider reverting.

Rafael Mendes: agreed. rolling back config first (safer than deploy rollback). @Aisha can you confirm if that change is expected?

Aisha Bello: checking audit logs now.

Aisha Bello: found it. change by routing-bot 18m ago tied to PR. likely intended for capacity test. not for prod us-east during peak :)

Miles Thornton: :grimacing: revert and monitor.

Rafael Mendes: reverted. watching error rate.

Sean Gallagher: ok circling back on bot: please add “fail-open” but *trustworthy*. if it can’t get data, tell us exactly why and what to do.

Jacob Stein: +1. I’ll implement:
- per-collector status with OK/PARTIAL/FAILED (x/y)
- show query window + newest sample timestamp when available
- if timeout: retry w/ smaller window + reduced labels
- if ingest lag detected: add one-line note
- move debug errors into main section (but keep it compact)

Allison Grant: tag me on PR; I’ll review wording/consistency with saturation standard.

Logan Wright: same. also pls keep time budgets bounded. last thing we want is bot DDOSing metrics during incidents.

Jacob Stein: yep. hard cap stays 8s total for saturation, with sub-queries sharing budget.

Sean Gallagher: cool. marking this thread as feedback for ENG-2845.

Rafael Mendes: errors dropping after revert. looks like config change was the trigger.

incident-bot: Responder feedback requested: react with :white_check_mark: if bundle was useful, :warning: if confusing, :x: if wrong.

Sean Gallagher: :warning: (saturation section confusing)

Aisha Bello: :warning:

Miles Thornton: :warning:

Logan Wright: :warning: (but fixable)

Jacob Stein: noted. thanks all.
